subject: Clarify host default retention: prompts vs outputs and EU residency
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acme-payments.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-payments.com
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: defaults for storing prompts/outputs & EU residency

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme's procurement team is triaging a few compliance items before we move to legal. Two quick questions we need to confirm for the SOW:

1) For Redwood's hosted API in the EU region, what are the default retention windows for: request metadata (timestamps, IPs), full request/response bodies (prompts + model outputs), and derived telemetry (embeddings, usage metrics)?

2) Are prompts and model outputs treated the same for retention? In other words, if a customer hasn’t enabled any storage options, will Redwood keep the plaintext prompts/outputs by default, and for how long?

We also need a short statement we can insert into the SOW about residency (i.e., data-at-rest location for EU customers) and expected deletion timelines once we issue a deletion request.

I've attached a short sample scope from our side to show where this language will go.

Thanks — if you can reply with concise bullets we can put directly into the procurement checklist.

Best,
Samantha Ruiz
Procurement Manager
Acme Payments

[Attachment: Acme-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ruiz <samantha.ruiz@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: defaults for storing prompts/outputs & EU residency

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below (concise bullets you can paste into the SOW). Attaching a short retention matrix for reference.

- Residency (short statement for SOW): For customers who select the EU-hosted region, Redwood stores data-at-rest and backups within EU data centers (primary and replicas), and processes requests in EU regions by default unless otherwise configured.

- Default retention (hosted, EU region):
  • Request metadata (headers, timestamps, non-sensitive telemetry): retained for 365 days for operational and billing analytics.
  • Request/response bodies (customer-provided prompts and returned model outputs): retained by default for 14 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and regression monitoring.
  • Derived telemetry (token counts, aggregation, embeddings used for service metrics): retained in aggregated or hashed form for 365 days.

- Prompts vs outputs: We do not treat prompts and outputs differently by default — both are categorized as request/response artifacts and are covered by the 14-day default retention window.

- Deletion request turnaround: For hosted customers, we offer a self-service deletion API for in-scope artifacts (see link below). Ad-hoc manual deletion requests submitted to support are processed within 48 hours; full replication/replica expiry and backup scrubbing may take up to 72 hours after deletion is applied.

- Dedicated & Private: If you plan to use Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, retention defaults are set by contract or by customer-managed config. We can set the default to a shorter window (e.g., 0/30 days) as part of the SOW amendment.

Actionable next steps for Acme (suggested SOW language you can paste):
  1) "Redwood will retain request/response artifacts (prompts and outputs) for a default period of 14 days in the EU-hosted region, unless otherwise agreed in writing."
  2) "Redwood will process deletion requests within 48 hours; permanent removal from primary storage and replicas may complete within 72 hours; backup snapshots may persist for an additional short window (up to 7 days) to preserve recovery capability."
  3) "For Dedicated or Private deployments, retention will be set by contract and may be configured to meet Acme's requirements."

Link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/retention-matrix-v2

Let me know if you want this tightened further for legal.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-retention-matrix-v2.pdf (summary matrix)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Mar 2028 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: defaults for storing prompts/outputs & EU residency

Jasmine — quick internal note to confirm before we finalize language for procurement/legal:

- The 14-day window for request/response bodies is accurate for hosted EU, but we should explicitly state that after 14 days we retain only hashed derivatives used for model-quality/regression telemetry unless a customer opts into longer retention. That helps when legal asks about reproduction of prompts later.

- Also confirm backup retention specifics: primary/replica wipe within 72 hours, but we've historically had weekly snapshots that could persist up to 7 days. We should not promise less than 7 days on backups without ops approval.

Can Neha confirm the backup snapshot SLA and whether we should include a line about backups possibly being retained short-term for disaster recovery?

Thanks — I can incorporate any tweaks into the SOW language.

—Priyom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: defaults for storing prompts/outputs & EU residency

Priyom — confirmed for hosted EU region:

- Primary data and synchronous replicas: deletion applied within 48 hours; final expiry across replicas typically completes within 72 hours.
- Scheduled backups/snapshots: retained for up to 7 days (we keep short-term snapshots for failover/recovery); we can include a contractual clause that allows a customer to request shorter snapshot retention subject to operational constraints.
- For the SOW language, recommend including the backup caveat exactly as: "Backups/snapshots may persist up to 7 days for disaster recovery; customers may request shorter snapshot retention and Redwood will evaluate operational feasibility."

I'll send a one-paragraph statement you can paste into the SOW and copy Legal if you want me to engage them.

Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
